- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect; apply a dampening factor (e.g., reduce forecast by 10–15% in the 2nd–3rd week post-spike).
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00 (neutral), model exhibits high volatility bias; apply a smoothing filter or reduce forecast variance by 20–30%.
- Mean reversion is strong in the 3rd–4th week of the forecast; if forecast is above 90% of historical mean, reduce by 5–8% per week until convergence.
- If sentiment history includes a single positive value (e.g., 0.40), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 5–10% in the following 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging the true trend; if true outcome shows a sharp drop after day 10–15, adjust forecast to reflect a 2–3 day lag in model response.
